back: High-pressure filtration in the glomerulus forcing water and small solutes into the Bowman's capsule, keeping cells and large proteins in the blood.

front: Three layers of the filtration barrier
back: Capillary endothelium (pores), basement membrane (main filter), podocytes (filtration slits).
Na⁺/K⁺ pump in basal membrane → low Na⁺ in cell → Na⁺ and glucose cotransported in → glucose diffuses out to blood.
Microvilli, many mitochondria, many cotransporters, tight junctions, close to capillaries.

front: Role of the loop of Henle
back: Countercurrent multiplier: creates a low water potential in the medulla so water can leave the collecting duct.
Low blood ψ → osmoreceptors (hypothalamus) → ADH from posterior pituitary → aquaporins in collecting duct → more water reabsorbed.

front: Where is ADH made and released?
back: Made in the hypothalamus; released from the posterior pituitary.
Glomerulus → Bowman's capsule → PCT → loop of Henle → DCT → collecting duct.
